newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: BHP approves Laminaria oilfield funding.
newsitem.headline: BHP approves Laminaria oilfield funding.

text.p: BHP Petroleum, a unit of Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd, said on Monday that it had approved its share of the development funding of the Laminaria and Corallina oil fields in the Timor Sea.
BHP said the development of the oil fields would cost a total of about A$1 billion.

Woodside Petroleum, the operator of the North West Shelf gas project, is also the operator of the oil fields located in the permit AC/P8 which is owned 50 percent by Woodside and 25 percent each by BHP and Shell Development (Australia) Pty Ltd.
BHP said the oil fields were estimated to have combined recoverable oil reserves of between 130 and 150 million barrels.
The Laminaria field extends into BHP's wholly-owned permit WA-260P.
BHP said the Laminaria development project would consist of the design, fabrication and installation of the world's biggest floating, production, storage and offloading (FPSO) facility.
The platform would be located in about 360 metres of water about 550 kilometres west northwest of Darwin.
